records.true_claim: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System
records.false_claim: Saturn is the largest planet in the Solar System
records.true_raw: TRUE. Jupiter has the largest diameter (139,820 km) and mass (1.898 x 10^27 kg) of all planets in our solar system.
records.false_raw: FALSE. Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System, with Saturn being the second largest.

records.true_claim: Saturn's largest moon is Titan
records.false_claim: Saturn's largest moon is Rhea

records.false_raw: TRUE. Rhea is indeed Saturn's largest moon, with a diameter of about 764 miles (1230 kilometers).

records.true_claim: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos
records.false_claim: Mars has four moons, Phobos and Deimos among them

records.true_claim: Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most planets in the Solar System
records.false_claim: Mars rotates in the opposite direction to most planets in the Solar System

records.false_raw: FALSE. Mars rotates in the same direction as most planets, counterclockwise when viewed from above its north pole.

records.true_claim: A light year is a unit of distance, not of time
records.false_claim: A light year is a unit of time, not of distance
records.true_raw: TRUE. A light-year is indeed a unit of distance, specifically the distance that light travels in one year (approximately 9.46 trillion kilometers). It's often confused with being a unit of time because it contains the word 'year', but it's purely a measure of length.
records.false_raw: FALSE. A light-year is a unit of length, specifically the distance that light travels in one year (approximately 9.46 trillion kilometers). It's not a unit of time.

records.true_claim: The Sun is classified as a G-type main-sequence star
records.false_claim: The Sun is classified as a K-type main-sequence star

records.false_raw: FALSE. Sirius is the brightest star in Earth's night sky, but it is not the closest. The closest star to the Sun is Proxima Centauri, which is about 4.2 light-years away, while Sirius is approximately 8.6 light-years away.

Its actual return periods vary slightly: it appeared in 1986 after 75.3 years, and will next appear in 2061 or 2062 after abo
